definition: Adaptive ML (often styled as Adaptive) is a private software company based in New York, United States and Paris, France.
details: The company focuses on reinforcement learning (“RLOps”), providing tools that allow organizations to customize and operate open-source large language models for specific applications.

explainer.lead: Adaptive ML is a software company that helps businesses customize open-source AI language models using reinforcement learning, rather than relying on generic third-party APIs. Founded in 2023 by researchers from Hugging Face and contributors to major open-source models, it was acquired by Datadog in June 2026.

tiers.eli5: Imagine you have a robot that can talk, but it only knows general stuff. Adaptive ML is like a workshop where you teach that robot to be really good at your specific job—say, answering your company's customer emails—by letting it practice and learn from feedback. Instead of renting someone else's robot, you get your own that keeps getting better the more you use it.
tiers.practitioner: Adaptive ML's platform, Adaptive Engine, provides reinforcement-learning-based post-training for open-source LLMs, targeting enterprises that need customization, privacy, and control. Typical applications include database query generation, automated customer-service workflows, and internal information retrieval systems. Pitfalls include the operational complexity of running your own model infrastructure and the need for continuous feedback loops to realize the promised adaptability.
tiers.paperLevel: Adaptive ML implements reinforcement learning operations ("RLOps") for post-training of open-source large language models, enabling organizations to perform domain-specific fine-tuning and continuous improvement through user interaction feedback. The founding team previously contributed to Falcon and BLOOM, and held research and engineering roles at Hugging Face. No formal algorithmic specification or originating paper is named in available sources.

explainer.example: A bank wants an AI that can answer complex questions about its internal loan policies. Using Adaptive Engine, it starts with the open-source Llama model, fine-tunes it on ten years of loan documentation and past customer inquiries, then deploys it to customer service representatives. Each time a representative corrects the model's answer or a customer satisfaction survey comes back, that signal feeds back into the training loop, and the model gradually becomes more accurate on that bank's specific terminology and edge cases.

usedIn.name: Database query generation
usedIn.detail: Adaptive Engine fine-tunes models to translate natural language into database queries for enterprise data systems.

usedIn.name: Automated customer-service workflows
usedIn.detail: Customized LLMs handle customer interactions with reinforcement learning from outcome feedback.

usedIn.name: Internal information retrieval
usedIn.detail: Models retrieve and synthesize proprietary organizational knowledge with domain-specific tuning.
